Sample a chosen number of circular spots within each target colony

Source: R/spots.R
sample_colony_spots.Rd

Whole-colony MI uses all eligible interior pixels. This optional measurement instead samples non-overlapping circular ROIs distributed by a deterministic farthest-point algorithm. The first centre is nearest the eligible-region centroid; later centres maximize separation. This is a reproducible spatial sample, not random sampling or a claim that it represents the entire colony. Placement is greedy, with at most 20,000 candidate centres; a shortage does not prove that an alternative geometric packing is impossible. ROIs lie entirely within the edge-excluded, non-specular target mask. Min/max are observed pixel extremes, not confidence limits. All spots are subsamples of the colony and plate, never independent biological replicates.

Usage

sample_colony_spots(
  result,
  n_spots = 5L,
  spot_radius_mm = 0.5,
  edge_exclude_mm = 0.1
)

Arguments

result

A funmel_result with images kept, or a segmented funmel_plate.

n_spots

Positive integer number of spots requested per target colony.

spot_radius_mm

Radius of each circular ROI, in mm.

edge_exclude_mm

Excluded target-colony rim, in mm.

Value

A list with spots (one row per achieved ROI) and summary (one row per expected colony). If the requested ROIs cannot fit, status is insufficient_space and summary MI_spot_mean/min/max are NA. Achieved ROIs remain available for inspection. No rim fallback or overlapping ROI is used.

Examples

sim <- simulate_plate(width = 300, height = 400, seed = 7)
res <- analyze_plate(sim$image, n_spots = 3, spot_radius_mm = 0.3,
                     n_boot = 20, verbose = FALSE)
res$spots
